title: DecisionModelBenchRecord
description: One committed measurement of a decision model against a fixed task set. The empirical history lives in bench/results.

taskSetSha.description: sha256 of the task file, so records are comparable only against the same labels

taskSetPath.description: Repo-relative path of the committed task file this sha names, so the rows behind a record are recoverable and it can be re-scored

ops.description: Op-level accuracy, including refusals. A refusal is coerced to `flag` so the ladder can still route it, which means every refused row that expected `flag` scores as a hit — with refusals > 0 these figures are partly refusal-derived and are an accuracy only when usableOutputRate > 0. Read usableOutputRate first; do not quote exactMatch or perOpRecall.flag from a record whose refusals approach its n, because always-flag reproduces them exactly.

selective.description: Accuracy if decisions below a confidence threshold are escalated. This is the number the ladder actually depends on.

regret.description: Cost-weighted score. The price of a wrong answer is read from matrix[expected][predicted] — there is no per-operation price. The costs are asserted and unitless, and a change of 1 to any weight reverses the ranking between variants, so weightsSwept is false and no ranking from this block is publishable until the matrix is swept.

matrix.description: The full expected x predicted cost table. Present so a reader can compute any policy's cost without reading the runner.

weightsSwept.description: False: the weights are asserted rather than fitted, so a variant ranking from them is not yet evidence. Absent from records written before the matrix was published.

baselines.description: The four constant policies scored on this record's own rows. The floor a model has to clear before its accuracy means anything: a record whose ops.exactMatch sits under baselines.alwaysNudge has not demonstrated signal. Absent from records written before the baselines were added.

refusals.description: Decisions where the model declined to pick an op. Not an error: a correct refusal routes to the escalator.

usableOutputRate.description: Share of rows on which the model produced a decidable op. When this is 0 the failure is upstream of scoring and ops.exactMatch is not measuring judgement.

accuracyGivenUsable.description: Accuracy over usable rows only. value is null when nothing was usable: with no denominator there is no accuracy to report, and 0 would invent one.

coverage.description: Row counts behind each per-op number: the sampled subset versus the whole corpus. A recall over 7 rows is not the same claim as a recall over 200.

baselineScore.description: One constant policy's score over the record's rows.
